text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today and has lost 11% over the past two weeks, a decline that tracks closely with the weakness in oil prices. US crude has retreated to $99.64 per barrel, while global oil trades at $107.03—meaningful drops that compress profit margins for oil producers. The stock was already under pressure after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th; absent a fresh catalyst, today's additional decline appears tied to ongoing softness in the broader energy complex.

The two-week selloff also reflects a shift in the political environment. News that voters rejected Trump and the GOP in the midterm elections has raised investor expectations that renewable energy policies will gain traction, which can dampen long-term demand outlooks for fossil fuel producers. While oil price weakness is the most direct daily driver, this political backdrop is part of the wider headwind pressuring energy stocks.
